thread:
jamie: Customer on eu-west reported a spike in latency (~250-600ms) and intermittent 401s. They sent a trace showing requests landing in us-west.
nina: Can you drop the dig +trace and the client's resolver IP so we can see EDNS/ecs behavior?
jamie: pasted trace from customer (redacted IPs):
```
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;api.redwood.ai. IN A
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.ai. 60 IN CNAME edge-lb.redwood.internal.
edge-lb.redwood.internal. 30 IN A 34.210.12.77
;; OPT PSEUDOSECTION:
; EDNS: version: 0, flags:; udp: 4096; COOKIE: 0000
```
jamie: customer resolver is an ISP that strips ECS according to their docs.
alex: If the resolver strips ECS, the upstream edge may serve a default-pop answer which can be us-west. That explains cross-region latency and token checks failing if auth token was region-aware (we have some legacy checks).
infra-bot: route-check: detected mismatched geoip-db version on edge-pop eu-central (db v2026-03-01 vs control-plane v2026-03-03). Some fallbacks to default-pop observed.
support-engineer: Seen a billing spike from the tenant for cross-region egress this morning — probably same root cause. Customer hit high token usage because retries increased.
nina: Quick repro steps: 1) run `dig +short @<customer-resolver> api.redwood.ai` 2) run `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:34.210.12.77 https://api.redwood.ai/status` 3) compare latency and auth headers. Share results.
jamie: did `dig` from an EU VM that uses the same ISP: got 34.210.12.77 (us-west) with TTL 30. After flushing local DNS cache, still same. Customer reported ISPs cache TTL longer than authoritative 60s.
alex: Workaround idea: push a temporary zero-TTL CNAME prefetch at the edge for the affected prefix so resolver prefers a eu-pop answer. Also we can relax region-bound auth for that tenant during mitigation (require ops approval).
support-engineer: For immediate relief I added a canary rollout to prefer eu-pop answers for that customer via routing override (service-route: prefer_region=eu, fallback=local). That dropped latency back to ~40ms and auth 401s stopped.
nina: We should also add a detection rule: if >10% of requests from a continent land outside continent for >5m, mark as geo-fallthrough and alert ops. Also add an ISP cache note to our onboarding docs.
jamie: Action items: - Alex to file infra ticket for geoip-db sync drift and add automated DB version checks (P1) - Nina to author runbook for resolver-strip cases with repro commands + mitigation steps (P2) - Support-engineer to send customer summary and temporary credit for egress spike (P2)
alex: Noted. For the ticket I'll include logs: `edge-pop-mapping` shows fallback_count=423 over 18m with majority from isp:FastNet-EU.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: routing-override canary applied to customer-id 98765 at 2026-03-16T15:12Z :thumbsup:
support-engineer: Customer confirmed restored perf and auth. They'll clear their ISP cache but asked for a longer-term fix so it doesn't reoccur after future geoip updates.
nina: We'll schedule a postmortem once infra ticket has preliminary root-cause. Keep thread updated. :memo:
